reviews.review: Great evolution of the DPG game into a Rouge lite. Super smooth, great graphics and excellent twitchy gameplay., My only ask would be for solo games give us a save for later feature. The missions take a bit of time, so this would be make it more pick up and play ready. Overall love DRG!
Do not get right now, needs a lot of work. It COULD be great but there are so many small/medium sized problems. Super easy for someone to grief a run.

Having sunk 750 hours into the original DRG and playing other roguelikes ofc i had to play this. Im really enjoying the game it feels pretty balanced I expected a slightly different game than DRG and they certainly delivered! Im glad its sufficiently different, its worth noting I mainly play co-op with friends so the solo experience may be different but its absolutely worth picking up. 

You will have some bad runs thats expected you will also have some good runs. Occasionally if your lucky you will have an incredible run, which will feel all the better for having the worse runs thats the idea!

Only things I would like to see is the option of longer runs and more outrageous powers and weapon combos. Many games chicken out on the "buffs" and water them down too much wheres the fun in that?

Rogue Core has really good bones for a game but there's issues that need to be fixed for it to be a more enjoyable experience.

Firstly, I do not get the obsession with games that had a shield system replacing it with an armor system in the following installment. The armor is brittle and weak and it feels like I'm just constantly at no armor or half armor as most attacks take a decent chunk of it out. Just go back to the shield system, it was way more enjoyable.

Ammo economy is another big issue with this game. You don't get a lot of ammo overall, even less if you dare to take a second weapon with you, and ammo resupplies are few and far between, usually only one at the start and one at the end. This is not inherently an issue, but enemies take a lot of damage before they die, especially the bigger threats. Again, by itself not an issue, but they compound into being I'm constantly at low or no ammo.

Drops being shared across all players is quite frankly, stupid. IT serves no point to allow all 4 players to pull from the same pool. What if two people want the same perk? Someone is getting it and someone isn't, and it serves no purpose but to add hostility into this team based game. DRG is a game that actively encouraged teamwork and companionship with your fellow Dwarf, whereas this game feels like it just is deliberately doing the opposite. Additionally removing the pass for perks to choose bonus health feels like such a random change that was not needed.

Runs also go on for a really long time, even the shorter runs can take a while. This is not a super issue, but I would like if there were options for runs to be under 20-ish minutes. It just sucks needing to dedicate like 40 minutes to a run, get bad rng and deal with frustrating balance and not get a win.

I understand it's an early access game and things are subject to change, but it feels like a lot of the lessons learned from DRG were just thrown out and we're starting fresh.

Cannot even begin to compare to original DRG. Very different game. Still has way too many issues (bugs, balancing, QoL) but some of the recent patches are making the game better imo.

If you like rogue-lite and shooters this might be the game for you under the condition you are ok with quite a mess. 

But there is a fair bit of highlights to the game. Classes are fun to play and feel strong... Some of the maybe a little too much (looking at you retcon)... A lot of fun ways to build your dwarves and upgrade your weapons. Still discovering new combos and new builds after 150+ hours so thats something I guess.

If the devs give up on the because of low players base then yeah I would have to change to not recommended but again. I feel like the game is heading in good direction.

My main issues with current state of the game:

1. Way too easy even on hardest difficulty: Game can be solo carried on highest difficulty by any class if the person has decent experience with average rolls.

2. Lack of level 6 missions on depth 04: If you like to play longer missions on highest difficulty then tough luck. You just might have to wait a couple hours before the game decides to roll one for you.

3. Retcon: I strongly believe this character is so stupid that after 2 levels Retcon can solo the entire mission. And by the end of the mission Retcon can solo while the rest of the team is trying to actively grief.

I had a lot of fun on this game for a while, getting through harder levels, and learning various characters. It feels a bit tedious after that, like what am I really accomplishing. There just isn't enough content for me to want to keep coming back right now. Maybe I will as the game gets out of early access, but its feels like it is missing something overall.

I really love this game so far, and the potential is pretty much infinite from here. While the game is in Early Access, it really isn't sloppy the way others make it out to be; there are annoying bugs from time to time but the more noticeable thing is a lack of features, which most certainly will change with time. I would most certainly not label this as "DRG 2" but more of a spinoff, as it has different mechanics than DRG, but still deeply part of the DRG universe with focus on new characters. I even think this game has the potential to be BETTER than the original game. If you love DRG and you're itching for better combat and longer missions, give this a shot. Just be weary of the leaf lovers who snatch up upgrades whether or not someone favorited them.

the game is fun. it takes a lot of assets from DRG but is much more akin to Risk of Rain in gameplay. lacks content right now, I probably wouldn't recommend it yet unless you're a big fan of DRG already. It has a long way to come in terms of polish and content. Two of the bosses feel really bad to fight currently (especially solo). I enjoy the timer and the feeling of urgency it gives, but it isn't for everyone. if you enjoy games that stress you out, you'll probably like this. It is not designed to be a chill experience.

If DRG OG was a 5/5, which by all my standards it was.  This is at best a 3/5.  I get the idea they were going for, the growing popular ‘rogue lite’ and ‘hardcore’.  But unfortunately, it just doesn’t translate as well.  The things that make this title unique, are also the things that may it annoying and frustrating (Monsters, Map Design, Match Length).
 This feels like it should have been a "Mode" add on for the original, like Deep Dives, instead of a standalone title.  The monsters are more annoying than unique.  The characters seem to be lopsided in terms of effectiveness, and everyone tends to blur as the match progresses due to random perks etc.  The "Omega" is a lifeless robot leader with no humor or soul.   It just feels flat, and replay ability in a title like this should be the main selling point but I find myself bored already, rise and repeat cycle just doesn’t have the same comradery as the prior version.  Player base is pretty low as well, maybe 4-5 servers running "D4" whenever I look.  I cant image future releases or content will fix the fundamental flaws.  It doesn’t take but ~20 hours or so to max out skill tree’s and unlock what’s available (Skins in this one are a joke).  Maybe another 10-15 to experiment with the different characters more but the stuff in the ship/lobby are lame, beers don’t provide perks.  

Done with this one, and hopefully for DRG #2 they expand the universe and mesh these titles.

As of now, it just doesn't have enough meat on its bones to justify the price tag.
It just feels like DRG, but you get a drip-feed of barely significant upgrades. I know this because I picked whatever and wasn't punished.
Also a multiplayer roguelite is also basically an oxymoron.
